question.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Reciprocal Function
question.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation:

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{4}+{20}^{∘})=2.
$$

The general solution of this equation is

$$
x={a}^{∘}+1\,{440}^{∘}\cdot n,\,x=1\,{120}^{∘}+1\,{440}^{∘}\cdot n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
question.worked_solution:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{4}+{20}^{∘})=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\frac{x}{4}+{20}^{∘}={60}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n,\,\frac{x}{4}+{20}^{∘}={300}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{4}=-{20}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n, & \,\frac{x}{4}=-{20}^{∘}+{300}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n \\ \frac{x}{4}={40}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n, & \,\frac{x}{4}={280}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n \\ x={160}^{∘}+1\,{440}^{∘}\cdot n, & \,x=1\,{120}^{∘}+1\,{440}^{∘}\cdot n.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have that $a=160.$
